title: Juice and satisfaction table

rows.quality or finding: Success-linked feedback, rather than mere amplification
rows.why it works (or fails): In the preregistered RPG experiment, outcomes mattered; occlusion is a proposed mechanism, not an isolated manipulation.
rows.effect size if known: n=1,699. Success-dependence → competence +.45 [95% CI .30,.60]; effectance +.26 [.15,.36]; curiosity +.29 [.17,.41]. Unstandardised scale-point coefficients.

rows.why it works (or fails): Tested non-success-dependent glow hid repeated impacts.
rows.how to make it: Audit action–outcome legibility before increasing volume.
rows.effect size if known: Amplification → effectance −.19 [−.36,−.03]; competence −.43 [−.68,−.19]. No significant direct enjoyment/playtime effect.

rows.quality or finding: Random variety is not established retention
rows.why it works (or fails): Variability did not significantly predict curiosity or playtime.
rows.how to make it: Use variation for appearance; test behavioural benefit.

rows.quality or finding: An intermediate amount can beat extremes
rows.why it works (or fails): One RPG bundled audiovisual changes, rather than isolating a particle setting.
rows.how to make it: Compare complete builds; no transferable medium/high particle budget.
rows.effect size if known: n=3,018. Partial η²: competence .005; autonomy .004; immersion .003; enjoyment .006; playtime .006; character level .006.

rows.why it works (or fails): None and Extreme both lost on playtime; enjoyment pairwise significance was Extreme < Medium/High, not None < Medium/High.
rows.how to make it: Do not equate statistical significance with a large retention improvement.
rows.effect size if known: Playtime F(3,3014)=5.83, p<.001; enjoyment F(3,3014)=5.87, p<.001. No numeric pairwise retention uplift found.

rows.quality or finding: Impact-feel features are candidates, not proven causes
rows.why it works (or fails): Review-derived game ranking plus descriptive feature inventory cannot isolate causes.
rows.how to make it: Test hit-stop, sound coherence and camera control separately.
rows.effect size if known: 281,720 Chinese reviews; 96 games, filtered to 44, then top/bottom 8 each. No causal effect size or feature correlation coefficient found.
rows.evidence level: preprint; JS03, A, 2022; later IEEE GEM publication verified

rows.why it works (or fails): In a minimal targeting task, words communicated graded performance more clearly.
rows.how to make it: Use readable success/outcome labels when needed; preserve meaning without particles.
rows.effect size if known: n=45; progress-feedback omnibus Kendall’s W=.44; means Text 5.62, Particles 4.43, None 2.81 (7-point scale).

rows.why it works (or fails): No overall superiority of text over juicy particles; observation/performance stages showed no significant performance differences.
rows.how to make it: Treat onomatopoeia as an optional style layer, not universal upgrade.
rows.effect size if known: Study effects lasted 0.5 s; this is stimulus duration, not optimal lifetime.

rows.why it works (or fails): Interviewed audio designers reserve standout moments, vary repetition and align sounds with visible events.
rows.how to make it: Keep frequent feedback restrained; let sound carry some impact.
rows.effect size if known: 12 expert interviews; no causal effect size, optimal variant count or repetition threshold found.

rows.quality or finding: Completion, fitting and clean endings as design targets
rows.why it works (or fails): Plausible perceptual/semantic goals; this search did not establish an effect-size recipe for them.
rows.how to make it: Specify an unambiguous terminal state and test whether it reads as complete.
rows.game uses: Coin counters, unlocks, assembly, UI success

intro: The best-supported conclusion is conditional: feedback must preserve action and outcome information. More decoration is not a universal route to enjoyment or motivation. Experimental effect sizes refer to the tested builds and samples.
